about: Himalaya Nutravedics manufactures, markets and distributes Ayurvedic and nutraceutical formulations in India and also does third-party contract manufacturing. It runs a single WHO-GMP facility in Hyderabad, sells through stockists across 17 states with a roughly 56-person field team, and own brands were 51.14% of FY26 revenue.
sector: Ayurvedic and nutraceutical formulations (pharma and wellness)

objects.purpose: Investment in branding, digital marketing and sales expansion

promoters.background: Promoters Rohit Asawa, Chanda Asawa, Rama Raju Penmatsa and Divya Asawa have given personal guarantees for the ICICI Bank cash credit facility. No promoter shares are pledged.

concentration.note: Top 10 customers were 81.24% of FY26 revenue (86.97% FY25, 84.19% FY24); top 10 suppliers were 94.30% of FY26 purchases and the top supplier alone 62.13%.

litigation_note: Income tax demand of Rs 27.26 lakh (Rs 0.27 crore) under Section 80-IAC disallowance, under appeal; this is the only contingent liability disclosed.
strengths: Revenue tripled from Rs 14.43 crore in FY24 to Rs 43.07 crore in FY26, with PAT growing from Rs 0.43 crore to Rs 7.39 crore.
EBITDA margin improved from 6.48% to 18.82% and PAT margin from 2.95% to 17.16% over FY24 to FY26.
Reported ROCE of 36.41% and RoNW of 45.12% in FY26.
Own-brand products were 51.14% of FY26 revenue, supported by a doctor-centric marketing model with about 56 sales staff.
Single integrated WHO-GMP facility with AYUSH and FSSAI licences and ISO, HACCP, Halal and Kosher certifications.
Presence across 17 states through a stockist-driven distribution network.
Debt to equity improved from 2.39 in FY24 to 0.31 in FY26 after equity raises.
Listed peers trade at P/E of 20.62 to 28.75 (average 24.68), giving a valuation reference.

risks.title: Heavy customer and supplier concentration
risks.detail: Top 10 customers were 81.24% of FY26 revenue, and the top 10 suppliers were 94.30% of purchases, with the top supplier at 62.13%. There are no long-term contracts with suppliers or customers.

risks.title: Negative operating cash flow
risks.detail: The RHP says operating cash flow was negative in FY24, FY25 and FY26 because of inventory and receivables build-up. FY26 operating cash flow was about minus Rs 3.74 crore against PAT of Rs 7.39 crore.

risks.title: High working capital intensity
risks.detail: Net working capital rose from Rs 2.87 crore in FY24 to Rs 17.49 crore in FY26. Receivables were 90 days and inventory 101 days at FY26; Rs 13.75 crore of the IPO goes to working capital.

risks.title: Tax holiday ending
risks.detail: Section 80-IAC tax benefit covers only FY25 to FY27, so profit after tax will fall once it expires. A Rs 27.26 lakh tax demand over this claim is under appeal.

risks.title: Single facility and leased premises
risks.detail: All manufacturing is at one leased site in Hyderabad, so disruption, lease termination or regulatory action would hit the whole business.

risks.title: Shift to D2C and branding spend
risks.detail: The company is moving from B2B to direct-to-consumer, and Rs 7.50 crore of IPO money goes to branding and marketing. Customer acquisition costs may pressure margins.

risks.title: Borrowings with promoter guarantees
risks.detail: Borrowings were Rs 5.32 crore as of August 14, 2026 (ICICI Bank cash credit, secured), guaranteed personally by four promoters.

risks.title: Small base, promoter dependence and no listed history
risks.detail: Company incorporated in 2022 with about 86 employees. Promoters hold 87.41% pre-issue, and some key managers have under a year of tenure and no listed-company experience.

notes: FY26 restated Indian GAAP standalone figures converted from lakhs to crore. Price band, issue size in rupees, P/E and post-issue promoter holding are blank in the RHP. Debt per D/E ratio calc (LT plus ST borrowings). FY24 operating cash flow left null because the garbled cash flow table conflicts with the risk factor stating it was negative. Reservation percentages are the maximum or minimum shares of the Net Issue (market maker portion of 1,26,000 shares excluded); the anchor portion sits inside the QIB portion. Peer CMPs not given. Post-issue shares equal pre-issue shares plus fresh issue.
